title: SEBI Data: Does Frequent Trading Actually Boost Returns?

faq.a: Equity derivatives are financial contracts whose value is derived from an underlying equity asset, such as individual stocks or stock market indices like Nifty or Sensex. Common types include futures and options.

faq.q: Why did SEBI conduct these studies?
faq.a: SEBI conducted these studies to understand the participation patterns and performance of individual investors in the equity derivatives market, aiming to inform policy decisions and enhance investor protection.

faq.q: Does SEBI recommend against trading in F&O?
faq.a: SEBI's studies highlight the significant risks and high probability of losses for individual traders in F&O. While SEBI does not outright ban F&O trading, it strongly advises caution, comprehensive understanding, and robust risk management for participants.

faq.q: Are all individual traders losing money in F&O?
faq.a: No, the studies indicate that a small percentage of individual traders do make profits. However, the vast majority (over 85-90%) incur losses, and the aggregate losses far outweigh the aggregate profits.

faq.q: How do transaction costs impact F&O trading profitability?
faq.a: Transaction costs, including brokerage, STT, exchange charges, and GST, are levied on every trade. For frequent traders, these costs accumulate rapidly and can significantly erode or even wipe out gross profits, leading to net losses even if individual trades are successful.

faq.q: Where can I find more information about SEBI's investor education initiatives?
faq.a: You can find more information about SEBI's investor education initiatives and advisories on their official website, particularly in the investor section.
